name: Made to Sew
shortDescription: Professional dressmaking technique — construction, fit and the finishes that separate a home-made garment from a made one.
longDescription: The channel states its subject as professional sewing and dressmaking: construction, fit, and couture-inspired finishing, using the methods of a working studio. {{longCountWords|cap}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads run over twenty minutes and the median is {{medianPhrase}}, which suits the material — a full garment sewn start to finish at thirty-four minutes, then short precise pieces on the individual operations that garment needed. A patch pocket done the way a shirt factory does it. A baby hem that stays flat on difficult fabric. How to assemble a printed pattern without the pieces drifting. The teaching is at the level of the operation rather than the project, which is what lets it transfer: the pocket method works on any shirt you ever make.
notFor: Anyone whose problem is a torn seam or a hem that needs taking up — this is garment construction, not repair, and the other creator here is the better first stop for mending. It also assumes a machine you are comfortable with.

categories.why: The 'making garments that actually fit' half of this category, taught at the level of the individual operation so it transfers beyond the project being demonstrated.
categories.evidence: 34 minutes sewing a complete garment step by step, 10 on a professional patch pocket, 8 on a baby hem that holds on difficult fabric, and 8 on assembling a printed pattern accurately.

entryVideo.title: How to Sew a Tie Neck Halterneck Top | Step-by-Step Sewing Tutorial
entryVideo.whyThisOne: A whole garment in one sitting, so you see how the separate operations sequence into something wearable — which no single-technique video can show you.

caveats: Studio-standard methods, which sometimes means more steps than a home sewer needs; the channel does not distinguish the essential from the refined. No teacher is named anywhere on the channel.

name: RJ The Bike Guy
shortDescription: An independent mechanic's repair archive — the jobs filmed as they actually go, on old bikes worth fixing rather than new ones worth selling.
longDescription: The channel has not posted since July 2025 and is listed for its back catalogue, which is a repair library rather than a broadcast. {{longCountWords|cap}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads pass twenty minutes and the median is {{medianPhrase}}. The jobs are the ones that actually strand people: overhauling a bottom bracket with sealed cartridge bearings, servicing a suspension fork down to disassembly and re-lubrication, replacing a recalled fork with a rigid one, and a fifty-nine-minute full overhaul of a free mountain bike from the state it was found in. Nothing is sponsored into the frame and nothing is new — the bikes are second-hand, the parts are what fits, and the reasoning includes when a repair is not worth doing.
notFor: Anyone with a current high-end bike looking for manufacturer-correct procedure; the other creator here is a tool maker and publishes exactly that. Also expect no updates — this is a closed archive, and components have moved on since.

categories.why: An independent mechanic working on ordinary second-hand bikes, against a tool manufacturer's channel — the same jobs, without the assumption that you own the right tool or a bike worth the right tool.
categories.evidence: 59 minutes overhauling a found mountain bike end to end, 24 replacing a recalled suspension fork, 14 servicing a fork through disassembly and re-lubrication, 10 rebuilding a bottom bracket, and 15 stripping a frame-damaged bike for usable parts.

entryVideo.title: Overhaul/Rebuild Bottom Bracket With Sealed Cartridge Bearings
entryVideo.whyThisOne: One of the routine jobs the category is named for, on the kind of bike most people actually own, in ten minutes and without a workshop.

caveats: QUIET SINCE JULY 2025 — this is an archive and will not answer a question about a current component. It is listed because the back catalogue teaches the routine jobs well and nothing is sold anywhere in it.
